title: Roast Turkey Thighs with Pan Gravy
subtitle: all the Thanksgiving turkey flavour for two, with crisp skin and real drippings gravy
imageAlt: Two golden roast turkey thighs with crisp skin on a cream plate with roasted carrots and a jug of gravy beside a navy napkin
servingsNote: Thanksgiving dinner for two, plus leftovers for sandwiches

beforeYouStart.text: Frozen thighs need about 24 hours in the fridge to thaw.
Pat the skin very dry and leave it uncovered in the fridge an hour if you can: crisper skin.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Pat the thighs dry. Mash the soft butter with the garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, dried thyme, dried sage, salt and pepper, and rub it under and over the skin.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Spread the onion, carrots and celery in a roasting pan or 23×33 cm (9×13 in) dish, set the thighs on top skin side up and roast 75–90 minutes, until the skin is deep golden and the thickest part reads at least 74°C (165°F); thighs are most tender at 80–82°C (175–180°F). Baste once halfway.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Move the turkey and vegetables to a platter and tent with foil 15 minutes.

steps.title: Gravy
steps.text: Pour the pan juices into a cup and spoon off all but 2 tbsp fat. Set the pan over medium, add the butter and that fat, whisk in the flour and cook 1 minute. Whisk in the broth and the juices, scraping up the browned bits, and simmer 5 minutes until thick. Season with salt.

steps.title: Carve
steps.text: Slice the meat off the bone and serve with the vegetables and gravy.

fixIt.fix: Turn the oven to 220°C (425°F) for the last 10 minutes.
Pour it through a sieve, or whisk hard over the heat.
Simmer 3–4 minutes more; it thickens as it reduces.

saleTip: Turkey thighs go on sale at No Frills the week before Thanksgiving; freeze a pack for later.
swap: Bone-in chicken thighs (roast 40–45 minutes to 74°C / 165°F). Turkey drumsticks work too.
leftovers: Turkey sandwiches with gravy, or into turkey soup.
doneness: Poultry pieces to at least 74°C (165°F) in the thickest part, not touching bone (Health Canada).
source: Based on tested roast turkey thigh and pan gravy methods (Canadian Living, America's Test Kitchen): butter-rubbed thighs roasted at 190°C on vegetables, drippings roux gravy.
gear: Roasting pan or 23×33 cm (9×13 in) dish
prepAhead: Season the thighs the night before and keep uncovered in the fridge.
Make the gravy ahead and reheat until bubbling.
reheat: Sliced turkey with a splash of gravy, covered, at 160°C (325°F) for 15–20 minutes or in the microwave, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Salt, pepper and garlic thighs with pan gravy; no vegetable bed.

stepNotes.1: Basic: roast the thighs straight in the pan.

fancy.note: A maple and apple cider glaze on the skin and cranberry sauce on the side.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: stir the maple syrup and vinegar and brush the skin for the last 15 minutes.

addSteps.title: Cranberry sauce
addSteps.text: Simmer the cranberries, sugar and ¼ cup water 8–10 minutes until the berries burst. Cool.

plating: Carve thick slices and fan them on warm plates.
Gravy in a jug, cranberry in a small bowl.

why.0-0: Thighs stay juicy where a whole bird's breast dries out, and roast in half the time.
why.0-1: Butter under the skin bastes the meat and crisps the skin.

funFact: Canadian Thanksgiving became a fixed national holiday on the second Monday of October in 1957.

keeps.note: slice and freeze with a little gravy

drink: An Ontario Pinot Noir or Chardonnay, or sparkling apple cider.
